text: His eyes asked her. <break time="0.8s" /> The question, Which. <break time="0.8s" /> There was not a moment. <break time="0.8s" /> To lose. <break time="0.8s" /> The princess raised her right hand. <break time="0.8s" /> A little and no one saw it. <break time="0.8s" /> Except the young man. <break time="0.8s" /> Without a pause. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked across the arena. <break time="0.8s" /> And opened the door. <break time="0.8s" /> On the right. <break time="0.8s" /> Now the point of the story is this. <break time="0.8s" /> Did the tiger come out of that door. <break time="0.8s" /> Or did the lady. <break time="0.8s" /> The more we think about it. <break time="0.8s" /> The harder it is to answer. <break time="0.8s" /> Night after night the princess had imagined him. <break time="0.8s" /> Torn by the tiger. <break time="0.8s" /> But more often she had imagined him. <break time="0.8s" /> Opening the other door. <break time="0.8s" /> And marrying the lady. <break time="0.8s" /> She hated. <break time="0.8s" /> She had seen his happy face. <break time="0.8s" /> And heard the wedding bells. <break time="0.8s" /> In her mind. <break time="0.8s" /> And she had cried in pain. <break time="0.8s" /> Would it not be better. <break time="0.8s" /> For him to die at once. <break time="0.8s" /> And wait for her. <break time="0.8s" /> In a better world. <break time="0.8s" /> She had thought about it. <break time="0.8s" /> For days and nights. <break time="0.8s" /> And she had made her decision. <break time="0.8s" /> I leave the question to you. <break time="0.8s" /> The reader which came out of the opened door. <break time="0.8s" /> The lady, or the tiger.
